stem: Precipitate Igniting Safety: When heating a wet filter paper containing a precipitate inside a porcelain crucible over a Bunsen burner, why must the crucible cover be left slightly ajar?
choices: To allow carbon monoxide to enter and reduce the precipitate.
To permit steam escape and prevent sudden pressure buildup/spattering.
To prevent atmospheric oxygen from oxidizing the precipitate.
To maintain a constant temperature inside the crucible.

stem:
Back-Titration Analysis: A $0.2000\text{-g}$ sample of impure ammonium sulfate, $\left( \text{NH}_{4} \right)_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$, is boiled with $50.00\text{~mL}$ of $0.1000\text{~M~NaOH}$ to drive off all $\text{NH}_{3}$ gas:

$$\left( \text{NH}_{4} \right)_{2}\text{SO}_{4} + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}_{2}\text{SO}_{4} + 2\text{NH}_{3}(g) + 2\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$$

The unreacted excess $\text{NaOH}$ requires $21.40\text{~mL}$ of $0.1000\text{~M~HCl}$ for neutralization. Calculate the percentage purity of the ammonium sulfate sample. ($\text{MW} = 132.14\text{~g/mol}$)

Water of Crystallization Determination: In a lab experiment, a student heats $2.497\text{~g}$ of hydrated copper(II) sulfate ($\text{CuSO}_{4} \cdot x\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$) in a crucible until constant mass. The anhydrous $\text{CuSO}_{4}$ remains as $1.596\text{~g}$. What is the experimentally determined value of $x$? ($\text{CuSO}_{4} = 159.6\text{~g/mol}$, $\text{H}_{2}\text{O} = 18.02\text{~g/mol}$)

Water Vapor Correction: A sample of oxygen gas is collected over water in a gas-measuring eudiometer tube at $23^{\circ}\text{C}$ and a barometric pressure of $754.0\text{~mmHg}$. The atmospheric pressure matches the internal gas height. If the vapor pressure of water at $23^{\circ}\text{C}$ is $21.1\text{~mmHg}$, what is the dry pressure of the oxygen gas?

Manometer Level Difference: An open-end liquid manometer filled with mercury ($\rho = 13.6\text{~g/cm}^{3}$) is connected to a gas bulb. The mercury level in the arm open to the atmosphere is $45\text{~mm}$ lower than the arm connected to the gas bulb. If atmospheric pressure is $755\text{~mmHg}$, what is the absolute gas pressure inside the bulb?

Dumas Method for Molar Mass: In a Dumas method experiment, a volatile liquid vaporizes at ${99.0}^{\circ}\text{C}$ in a $250.0\text{-mL}$ flask at an atmospheric pressure of $0.985\text{~atm}$. The mass of the condensed vapor inside the flask is $0.684\text{~g}$. What is the molar mass of the compound?

Victor Meyer Method Error: In the Victor Meyer apparatus for molar mass determination of volatile liquids, if a few drops of the sample fail to vaporize completely inside the heated inner tube, how does this affect the calculated molar mass?
choices: The calculated molar mass will be higher than the true value.
The calculated molar mass will be lower than the true value.
The calculated molar mass will remain unaffected.
The gas volume displaced will be artificially increased.

stem: Eudiometer Height Adjustment: When measuring the volume of hydrogen gas collected over water in a eudiometer tube, the water level inside the tube is $6.8\text{~cm}$ higher than the water level outside in the beaker. If $13.6\text{~mm~H}_{2}\text{O} = 1.00\text{~mm~Hg}$, what correction must be applied to the barometric pressure to find the total gas pressure inside the tube?

Gas Effusion Apparatus Calibration: A student uses a Schloesing effusion apparatus to measure the effusion rate of an unknown gas relative to argon ($\text{MW} = 39.95\text{~g/mol}$). The argon gas takes $48.2\text{~s}$ to effuse through a microscopic orifice, while the same volume of unknown gas takes $64.1\text{~s}$ under identical temperature and pressure. What is the molar mass of the unknown gas?

Gas Generation Safety: When producing acetylene ($\text{C}_{2}\text{H}_{2}$) gas in a lab setting by adding water to calcium carbide ($\text{CaC}_{2}$), why is a gas washing bottle containing acidified copper(II) sulfate ($\text{CuSO}_{4}$) solution placed in the gas collection line?
choices: To remove phosphine ($\text{PH}_{3}$) and hydrogen sulfide ($\text{H}_{2}\text{S}$) impurities.
To catalyze the combustion of acetylene.
To act as a liquid seal to prevent back-suction of oxygen.

stem: Gas Syringe Reading: A gas syringe is used to record gas evolution kinetics. At $25^{\circ}\text{C}$, the friction of the syringe plunger introduces a small resistive force corresponding to $+ 15.0\text{~Torr}$ extra pressure inside the syringe. If the barometric pressure is $750.0\text{~Torr}$, what is the true gas pressure driving the expansion?

Ideal vs Real Gas Lab Deviation: A laboratory gas cylinder filled with carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_{2}$) at high pressure ($50\text{~atm}$) is opened slightly, releasing gas into a ambient plastic vessel. The temperature of the released gas near the nozzle drops noticeably. This cooling effect (Joule-Thomson expansion) occurs primarily because:
choices: The gas does work overcoming attractive intermolecular forces (Van der Waals $a$ constant).
The molecular volume of the gas molecules expands rapidly (Van der Waals $b$ constant).
Kinetic energy is converted directly into potential energy of covalent bonds.
Air surrounding the nozzle absorbs heat from the expanding gas.

stem: Stoichiometry of Gas Generation: A student decomposes a $0.400\text{-g}$ mixture of $\text{KClO}_{3}$ and $\text{KCl}$ in the presence of $\text{MnO}_{2}$ catalyst by heating. The evolved $\text{O}_{2}$ gas is collected, occupying $68.5\text{~mL}$ at $22^{\circ}\text{C}$ and $740.0\text{~mmHg}$ (dry). What is the percentage of $\text{KClO}_{3}$ ($\text{MW} = 122.55\text{~g/mol}$) in the initial sample?
Drying Agents for Gases: Which of the following drying agents is unsuitable for drying gaseous ammonia ($\text{NH}_{3}$) in a laboratory purification train?

Barometer Temperature Correction: A mercury barometer reads $762.4\text{~mm}$ at a room temperature of $28^{\circ}\text{C}$. Given that the thermal expansion coefficient of mercury is $\beta = 1.82 \times 10^{- 4}\text{~K}^{- 1}$, what is the corrected barometric height at standard temperature ($0^{\circ}\text{C}$)?

Gas Leak Detection Technique: In high-vacuum laboratory systems containing helium gas, small pinhole leaks are localized using a mass spectrometer leak detector (MSLD). Why is helium chosen as the tracer gas?
choices: Helium has a high polarizability making it easy to ionize.
Helium has a small atomic radius, low background atmospheric concentration, and fast effusion rate.
Helium reacts rapidly with air to produce visible optical fluorescence.
Helium condenses easily at ambient temperatures.

stem: Coffee-Cup Calorimeter Heat Capacity: To measure the heat capacity of a polystyrene coffee-cup calorimeter, $50.0\text{~mL}$ of hot water at ${60.0}^{\circ}\text{C}$ is added to $50.0\text{~mL}$ of cold water at ${20.0}^{\circ}\text{C}$ inside the cup. The final equilibrium temperature is ${38.5}^{\circ}\text{C}$. Taking the specific heat of water as $4.184\text{~J/(g} \cdot^{\circ}\text{C)}$ and density as $1.00\text{~g/mL}$, what is the heat capacity of the calorimeter ($C_{cal}$)?

Heat of Solution Measurement: In a coffee-cup calorimeter ($C_{cal} = 25.0\text{~J/}^{\circ}\text{C}$), $8.00\text{~g}$ of ammonium nitrate ($\text{NH}_{4}\text{NO}_{3}$, $\text{MW} = 80.04\text{~g/mol}$) is dissolved in $100.0\text{~g}$ of distilled water, both initially at ${22.0}^{\circ}\text{C}$. The temperature drops to ${16.5}^{\circ}\text{C}$. Assuming the specific heat of the solution is $4.18\text{~J/(g} \cdot^{\circ}\text{C)}$, calculate the molar enthalpy of solution ($\Delta H_{soln}$) for $\text{NH}_{4}\text{NO}_{3}$.

Bomb Calorimeter Calibration: Benzoic acid ($\text{C}_{7}\text{H}_{6}\text{O}_{2}$) is used as a standard for calibrating bomb calorimeters. Its heat of combustion is known to be $- 32.27\text{~kJ/g}$. When $1.152\text{~g}$ of benzoic acid is burned in excess oxygen in a bomb calorimeter, the temperature rises by ${3.125}^{\circ}\text{C}$. What is the heat capacity of the calorimeter assembly ($C_{cal}$)?

Enthalpy of Neutralization (Polyprotic Acid): When $50.0\text{~mL}$ of $1.00\text{~M}\text{~H}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}$ is reacted with $100.0\text{~mL}$ of $1.00\text{~M~NaOH}$ in a calorimeter, the heat released is $5.71\text{~kJ}$. What is the molar enthalpy of neutralization expressed per mole of water formed?
